title: Protocols of 3D Bioprinting of Gelatin Methacryloyl Hydrogel Based Bioinks
protocol: Prepare Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM) with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Culture human breast cancer cell lines (MDA-MB-231) in the prepared DMEM.
Passage MDA-MB-231 cells at a ratio of 1:2 when they reach 90% confluence.
Prepare DMEM/F-12 with L-glutamine, supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Culture human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) lines in the prepared DMEM/F-12.
Passage HUVEC cells at a ratio of 1:2 when they reach 90% confluence.
Prepare bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) culture medium by supplementing DMEM with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Culture BMSC lines in the prepared culture medium.
Passage BMSC cells at a ratio of 1:2 when they reach 90% confluence.
Print a fixture using polylactic acid (PLA) on a fused deposition modeling (FDM) printer.
Place two metal ring electrodes into the printed fixture.
Connect one metal ring electrode to the ground pole and the other to the positive pole.
Position a Petri dish containing silicon oil above a metal plate connected to the high voltage below the ring electrode.
Dissolve freeze-dried GelMA (5% w/v) and lithium phenyl-2,4,6-trimethylbenzoylphosphinate (LAP, 0.5% w/v) in Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS).
Filter the bioink through a 0.22 μm filter for sterility.
Heat the filtered bioink at 37 °C in a water bath for 15 min.
Detach MDA-MB-231 cells using 3 mL of trypsin-EDTA solution (0.25% trypsin, 0.02% EDTA) for 3 min at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the detached cells in a 15 mL centrifugal tube at 100 x g for 5 min to obtain a cell pellet.
Remove the supernatant.
Mix the cell pellet with 1 mL of prepared bioink by slowly pipetting to prevent bubble formation.
Place 1 mL of bioink (MDA-MB-231) into a 3 mL sterile syringe.
Feed the bioink using compressed air (~0.5 kPa).
Put the syringe on the fixture.
Switch on the high voltage power and set the voltage as 0−4 kV.
Simultaneously, turn on the 405 nm wavelength light to crosslink GelMA droplets in silicon oil.
Pour most of the silicon oil away by decanting the Petri dish.
Transfer the remaining silicon oil and GelMA microspheres into a 15 mL centrifugal tube using a spoon.
Add 5 mL of DPBS and shake the mixture uniformly.
Centrifuge the tube at 100 x g for 5 min and remove the supernatant fluid.
Repeat step (centrifugation) 3 times.
Take out the GelMA microspheres with a spoon.
Culture the microspheres in DMEM in a Petri dish at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Discard the medium and wash the microspheres with DPBS.
Fix the microspheres with 2 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 30 min at room temperature (RT).
Discard the PFA and wash the microspheres with DPBS.
Permeabilize the microspheres with 2 mL of 0.5% nonionic surfactant (i.e., Triton X-100) for 5 min at RT.
Discard the nonionic surfactant and wash the microspheres with DPBS.
Stain the microspheres with 2 mL of tetramethylrhodamine (TRITC) phalloidin for 30 min in darkness at RT.
Discard the TRITC and wash the microspheres with DPBS.
Stain the microspheres with 2 mL of DAPI for 10 min in darkness at room temperature.
Discard the DAPI and wash the microspheres with DPBS.
Capture the morphology of the microspheres using a confocal fluorescence microscope.
Prepare a coaxial nozzle as shown.
Fix an inner nozzle (25 G) and outer nozzle (18 G) with soldering.
Connect a glass tube to the end of the coaxial nozzle.
Dissolve sodium alginate powder in deionized water at 2% (w/v).
Sterilize the sodium alginate solution under ultraviolet light for 30 min.
Prepare a sterile bioink solution following step 2.3.
Heat the GelMA bioink and Na-Alg solution in a 37 °C water bath for 15 min.
Detach BMSCs cells with 3 mL of trypsin-EDTA solution for 3 min at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the cells in a 15 mL centrifugal tube at 100 x g for 5 min to obtain a cell pellet.
Remove the supernatant fluid from the cell pellet.
Mix the cell pellet with 2 mL of prepared GelMA bioink by slowly pipetting it.
Place 2 mL of bioink (BMSCs) into a 10 mL syringe.
Place 2 mL of Na-Alg solution into another syringe (10 mL).
Feed the bioink and Na-Alg solution with two syringe pumps, respectively.
Turn on the 405 nm wavelength light to irradiate the transparent tube for crosslinking GelMA fibers.
Place a Petri dish with DPBS to receive the fibers.
Remove the GelMA fibers from DPBS using a spoon and culture them in prepared DMEM/F-12 at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Prepare GelMA fibers for morphological observation with a confocal fluorescence microscope following steps 2.12−2.16.
Wipe the DLP bioprinter with 75% alcohol.
Expose the DLP bioprinter to UV irradiation for 30 min.
Dissolve freeze-dried GelMA (10% w/v) and LAP (0.5% w/v) in DPBS.
Add magenta edible pigment into the solution (3% v/v).
Filter the solution through a 0.22 μm filter.
Heat the filtered solution in a 37 °C water bath for 15 min.
Build 3D models with CAD software.
Import model documents to the upper software of the DLP bioprinter.
Add 10 mL of prepared bioink into the trough of the DLP bioprinter.
Set printing parameters: light intensity = 12 mW/cm², irradiation duration = 30 s, slice height = 100 μm.
Start printing.
Remove the printed structure from the bioprinter.
Immerse the printed structure in DPBS in a Petri dish.
Detatch MDA-MB-231 cells with 3 mL of 0.25% trypsin-0.02% EDTA for 3 min at 37 °C.
Centrifuge cells at 100 x g for 5 min in a 15 mL tube to obtain a cell pellet.
Remove the supernatant fluid and mix the cell pellet with 2 mL of DMEM.
Add 100 μL of cell suspension onto printed structures.
Culture cells on the structures for 3 days in prepared DMEM at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Dissolve freeze-dried GelMA (10%, w/v) and LAP (0.5%, w/v) in DPBS.
Filter the GelMA solution through a 0.22 μm filter for sterility.
Sterilize gelatin powder under UV light for 30 min.
Add sterilized gelatin to the GelMA-LAP solution to achieve a final concentration of 5% (w/v).
Heat the mixture in a 37 °C water bath for 15 min.
Design molds with CAD software and manufacture them with photopolymer resin on a DLP printer.
Fill the molds fully with prepared bioink.
Put the molds into a 4 °C refrigerator to crosslink the gelatin for 30 min.
Remove the molds and demold partially crosslinked hydrogel sheets from the molds with a blade.
Combine two demolded hydrogel sheets and bond them by irradiating at 405 nm for 1 min.
Detach HUVECs cells with 3 mL of 0.25% trypsin-0.02% EDTA solution for 3 min at 37 °C.
Centrifuge cells in a 15 mL centrifugal tube to obtain a cell pellet at 100 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant fluid and mix the cell pellet with 2 mL of DMEM.
Fill the microchannel fully by injecting the cell suspension with a nozzle and syringe.
Flip the chip upside down every 15 min during the next 3 h to achieve uniform and complete cell seeding.
Culture the chips in the Petri dish for 3 days in the prepared DMEM at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
